archetype: fenced industrial vehicle scrapyard with intake office, dismantling shop, parts warehouse and sorted salvage yards
ground_program: north main-road entrance with gatehouse and inbound vehicle inspection lane
customer and hauler office with reception window, records desk and staff-only yard access
vehicle scale and intake lane positioned before the dismantling and storage yards
covered dismantling workshop with two vehicle work bays, fluid-drain station and tool storage
secure reusable-parts warehouse with shelving, tagged component racks and loading door
outdoor incoming-vehicle rows separated from stripped-shell and processed-scrap zones
sorted ferrous, non-ferrous, tire and reusable-component storage areas with physical separation
mobile-crane or material-handler work zone with a clear swing envelope and reinforced hardstanding
battery, fuel, oil and coolant quarantine area protected from ordinary scrap piles
staff locker, washroom and break space attached to the office/workshop complex
south secondary service gate providing an independent hauler exit and emergency access
perimeter fencing, lighting and service paths that keep public customers out of active dismantling zones
graded industrial hardstanding with drainage channels, containment sumps and a road apron feathered into surrounding terrain
upper_program: partial office mezzanine overlooking the intake scale and main yard circulation
parts-warehouse catwalk serving high storage racks without crossing vehicle work bays
no general occupied upper floor over the open scrap-processing yard
circulation: incoming vehicles enter from the north gate, pass inspection and scale, then follow a one-way yard loop to intake, dismantling or storage
outbound haulers leave through the south service gate so loaded trucks do not reverse through the customer entrance
customers remain in the office and designated parts-pickup edge while staff use controlled doors into the yard
mechanics move directly between dismantling bays, fluid quarantine, tools and reusable-parts warehouse
material-handling equipment has a continuous yard route linking vehicle rows, processing zones and sorted scrap piles without crossing pedestrian waiting space
the office mezzanine and warehouse catwalk use supported stairs with real landings and continuous headroom
damage_constraints: preserve both north and south gates and enough of the one-way yard loop to keep the site's intake-to-processing flow legible
preserve at least one dismantling bay, the parts warehouse and the hazardous-fluid quarantine area
concentrate major building failure on one workshop/warehouse corner with an irregular fracture and gravity-led debris rather than rectangular deletion
allow localized fence collapse and displaced scrap to spill toward damaged edges without blocking every surviving route
keep crane or material-handler remains structurally supported and associated with its reinforced work zone
damage catwalks, stairs, signs and attached fixtures together with their supporting structure so no floating fragments remain
retain differentiated vehicle, shell, metal, tire and hazardous-material zones after damage
derive damaged and occupied variants only from this immutable clean master

required_manual_checks: the site reads as an operating scrapyard and dismantling business rather than a random field of scrap blocks
intake, scale, dismantling, reusable-parts, processed-scrap and hazardous-fluid functions are spatially distinguishable
customer, staff, hauler and material-handler circulation are coherent and player-scale usable
the north entrance and south service gate connect to a believable one-way industrial yard flow
stairs and catwalks are supported, enclosed where required, have headroom and terminate on real floors or platforms
hardstanding, drainage, containment and perimeter treatments transition credibly into surrounding terrain
damage follows structural gravity while preserving enough operational evidence to infer the original scrap-processing workflow
